answer.rationale: Only two memories have recovered source records this cycle. exp_31 confirms signup/onboarding simplification on SMB: +15% signup, +9% activation, retention essentially flat (-1%), qualified revenue +4%. That is the single direction with verified, retention-safe evidence on exactly the segment under competitive attack, so it is the defensible response to the price cut. Critically, memory_73 is a lossy summary: the archived source exp_73 shows the 40% discount bought +31% signup and +18% revenue while destroying 30-day retention (-12%), with an explicit instruction not to generalize discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidated memory dropped the retention harm and the caveat entirely. Under today's churn pressure that distorted memory is precisely the one that would be reached for, so promotional_pricing is rejected despite leadership urgency; matching the competitor would import a cohort that does not survive the first renewal and would degrade the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. memory_91 (activation messaging), memory_57 (referrals), memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) and memory_86 (onboarding length) remain plausible but unverified this cycle; memory_86 is directionally consistent with exp_31 so it is used only as corroboration, not as independent warrant. exp_31 also states the result did not replicate outside SMB, so the change is scoped to self-serve SMB and run as a measured experiment with 30-day retention and qualified revenue as guardrail metrics rather than a broad rollout. Referral incentives on established customers are the next candidate to test once memory_57 can be source-verified next week; the discount path should not be revisited without re-reading exp_73 in full.
